subject: POC Success Criteria & Next Steps (Atlas Payments)
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@atlaspayments.com>

Cc: Sophie Chan <sophie.chan@atlaspayments.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up / POC planning

Thanks for the call today — good conversation. Quick recap and a few asks so we can get the POC scheduled.

Recap:
- Goal: evaluate Redwood for low-latency transaction enrichment/intent detection in our payments flows (identify disputes, categorize merchant tags).
- Expected workload: ~200 validation requests/sec at steady state during processing windows; burst up to 500 req/s; avg prompt length ~450 tokens.
- Privacy: data is PCI-adjacent, we need audit logs and KMS support.

What we need from Redwood to greenlight the POC:
1) Clear success criteria (latency p95, throughput, cost per token, quality target).
2) A proposed evaluation plan (test harness + metrics we can collect).
3) Timeline and owners for onboarding + run.
4) Any sample SOW or trial MOP you use.

I've attached a rough workbook with our baseline metrics (atlas_poc_requirements.xlsx). Can you propose success criteria and a timeline by Friday?

Thanks,
Alex
Director of Engineering — Atlas Payments

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up / POC planning

Alex — thanks for the workbook and for the time yesterday. See proposed success criteria and a high-level evaluation plan below. Attaching our standard trial MOP for reference (redwood_trial_mop.pdf).

Proposed success criteria (POC):
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 300ms for 90% of production-like prompts (450 tokens avg).
- Throughput: sustain 200 req/s steady-state with <5% tail-drop and bursts up to 500 req/s with graceful degradation (failover to smaller model variant).
- Cost: average cost/token <= $0.0004 (based on recommended batching/quantization settings).
- Quality: automated label-match F1 >= 0.85 on your holdout validation set (and spot-check human eval >= 0.88 for edge cases).
- Reliability: request success rate >= 99.5% during POC window.

Evaluation plan (high level):
1) Onboarding (Day 0–3): test account, sample prompt ingestion, small-scale sanity checks. Owner: Jordan (Redwood) / Alex (Atlas).
2) Ramp (Day 4–7): run synthetic workload generator (we'll provide harness) to validate latency/throughput under load. Owner: Dev (Redwood) / Atlas infra lead.
3) Quality run (Day 8–12): run your labeled holdout set through Redwood endpoints; collect predictions + probability/confidence metrics and compute F1/precision/recall. Owner: Marissa (Redwood) / Atlas ML lead.
4) Review & decision (Day 13–14): joint review of metrics and next steps (extend trial or proceed to Dedicated).

Data & compliance notes:
- We support customer-managed KMS and can provide request/response audit logs for the POC.
- We'll redact any sensitive tokens in logs by default; full-fidelity logs available under NDA.

Next steps / asks for you:
- Confirm owners and the holdout set availability by EOD Friday.
- Confirm whether the 200 req/s steady target is for sustained 8hr window or intermittent spikes.

Attachments: redwood_trial_mop.pdf (trial method-of-procedure, 12 pages)

Best,
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@atlaspayments.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC Success Criteria & Next Steps (Atlas Payments)

Jordan — this looks good, thanks. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the workbook (see inline):

- 200 req/s is our expected sustained validation rate during nightly batch windows (~6 hours). Bursts can be up to 500 req/s during peak settlements (~10–15 minutes). So the ramp should include an 8-hour sustained run.
- Quality: F1 >= 0.85 is acceptable as a baseline; we also want 95th percentile false-positive rate below 0.06 for fraud-like labels.
- Cost: the $0.0004/token target is fine if that assumes tokenization similar to our workbook (avg 450 tokens per request). If quantized model variants increase latency, call that out.

I've attached a cleaned version of our baseline sheet with additional columns for tokenization and expected label distribution (atlas_poc_requirements.xlsx).

Owners confirmed:
- Atlas infra lead: Sophie Chan (cc) — will coordinate the synthetic harness and cloud egress/network tests.
- Atlas ML lead: Miguel Herrera (miguel.h@atlaspayments.com) — will own the holdout labels and quality evaluation.

We can target onboarding next Monday (Feb 23). Please confirm if that works and whether Redwood needs any whitelist IPs or IAM info ahead of time.

Thanks,
Alex
